items.quote: Intervention for the prevention and control of osteoporosis should comprise a combination of legislative action, educational measures, health service activities, media coverage, and individual counselling to initiate changes in behaviour.
items.author: Gro Harlem Brundtland

items.title: A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment
items.abstract: This paper introduces Comparison-based Preference Optimization (ComPO), a novel zeroth-order method for aligning LLMs with human preferences. Instead of relying on direct optimization of differentiable losses, ComPO extracts directional information from preference pairs using comparison oracles. This approach offers computational efficiency and provides a convergence guarantee, with an online variant further enhancing its applicability.

items.title: CERA-MoA: Co-Evolving Routing Mechanisms with Continually Learning LLM Agents
items.abstract: CERA-MoA introduces a novel iterative reinforcement learning framework that co-evolves a dynamic router with continually learning LLM agents. Its core contribution is a predictive familiarity estimator that uses mid-layer hidden states to assess agent competence, enabling a cumulative-threshold adaptive routing mechanism to dynamically select a minimal agent subset for efficient and performant task execution.

items.title: Cognitive Extensions for Dual-Process Language Agents: Memory and Self-Reflection in Interactive Environments
items.abstract: This paper introduces cognitive extensions, an Adaptive Memory Module (AMM) and a Self-Reflection Module (SRM), to enhance dual-process language agents in interactive environments. The AMM provides salience-gated memory, while the SRM offers execution-time validation and correction. The full system, incorporating both modules, significantly improves performance on tasks requiring long-horizon reasoning and error recovery, with the SRM proving to be a particularly impactful standalone contribution.
items.figure_caption: Full-system architecture. SwiftSage remains the action-selection substrate; AMM adds salience-gated episodic writing and trigger-driven retrieval; SRM adds Gate–1 validation, stagnation detection, and bounded Critic correction before actions reach ScienceWorld.

items.title: Higher-order pruning of experts in mixture-of-experts language models
items.abstract: This paper introduces HOPE (Higher-Order Pruning of Experts), a novel method for reducing the parameter count in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models. Unlike prior methods that prune experts independently, HOPE considers the cooperative nature of expert usage by employing a second-order pruning objective. This approach provably minimizes an upper bound on pruning error, leading to superior pruning decisions and significant parameter reduction, especially at high pruning rates.

items.title: Hypothesis-Driven Autonomous Materials Synthesis with Multimodal LLM Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces SynAgent, a framework for autonomous materials synthesis that uses multimodal Large Language Model (LLM) agents. Unlike traditional black-box optimizers, SynAgent's core method involves the LLM agents maintaining and evolving an explicit, hypothesis-driven understanding of the synthesis process. Its key contribution is enabling the LLM to adaptively generate analysis skills and reason multimodally over experimental data, guided by a verify-falsify scheme, to achieve autonomous discovery with articulated reasoning.
items.figure_caption: Overview of the SynAgent framework. a , The four-step autonomous loop of experiment proposal (Step 1), synthesis and measurement (Step 2), skill-based data analysis (Step 3), and reflection with understanding update (Step 4), where all reasoning is performed by multimodal LLM agents. b , Adaptive skill generation: when no suitable skill exists in the skill library, the main agent delegates to a subagent that creates and registers a new one, and the registered skills are reused in later iterations. c , Evolving understanding through verify–falsify reasoning: each proposal is designed to either verify or falsify the current understanding, and the reflection on the experimental outcome reinforces or revises it, progressively evolving the understanding over the course of the campaign.

items.title: Recursive Reasoning or Statistical Extrapolation? In-Context Learning in Multi-Agent Interdependent Decision-Making
items.abstract: This paper investigates whether in-context learning (ICL) in LLM agents performing interdependent decision-making relies on genuine reasoning or statistical pattern extrapolation. By testing LLM agents in games with manipulated historical feedback, they found that disrupting statistical patterns significantly degrades decision quality. This suggests that ICL in these strategic environments primarily acts as statistical extrapolation rather than sophisticated reasoning.
items.figure_caption: Relational Complexity in Multi-Agent Systems. When everyone is constantly influencing everyone else, making a single decision becomes an overwhelming task. This structure necessitates a shift from simple logic to a deep and complicated cycle of guessing what others might do, highlighting the challenge of strategic coordination.

items.title: STRETCH the Boundaries: A Unified Self-Taught Framework for Progressive LLM Evolution
items.abstract: STRETCH is a unified framework for progressive LLM self-improvement that addresses capability stagnation by dynamically adjusting challenge difficulty. Its core method, the Stretch Zone mechanism, uses a dual-loop co-evolution of a Scaffolder and a Learner within a single parameter space. This approach promotes stable training, prevents reward hacking, and fosters continuous reasoning growth, outperforming existing baselines on various benchmarks.
items.figure_caption: Motivation of the STRETCH Framework. (a) Cognitive Zones: Comfort, stretch (optimal learning), and difficulty. (b) Paradigm Comparison: Top: static general questions leading to learner capability stagnation. Bottom: adaptive questions achieving dynamic difficulty matching via a learnable Scaffolder for progressive improving of Learner.

items.title: Ask the Tool, Don't Guess: Agent Tool Calls Hold Their Progress, and the Serving System Should Read It
items.abstract: This paper addresses the inefficiency of agent systems waiting for tool execution by proposing that tools explicitly report their progress. Instead of guessing tool durations, the system can dynamically manage GPU memory based on real-time progress signals. This approach recovers valuable KV cache memory without negatively impacting agent performance.

items.title: ASLEval: Measuring Privacy Exposure Displacement in LLM Agent Sessions
items.abstract: This paper introduces "privacy exposure displacement" to address limitations in evaluating LLM agent privacy. Their framework, ASLEval, measures the mismatch between local privacy checks and actual data exposure across multi-step sessions. This approach reveals significant privacy leaks missed by traditional methods, highlighting issues with outlet-only views and attacker reports.

items.title: Beyond Outcomes: Dual-View Relational Learning for Efficient Agent Benchmarking
items.abstract: This paper introduces DualViewEval, a novel method for compressing agent benchmarks. It addresses the high cost of evaluating agents by jointly learning from both final outcomes and complementary process signals observed in agent trajectories. This dual-view approach allows for more efficient and accurate prediction of full benchmark scores using a significantly smaller subset of tasks.

items.title: Beyond Truncation: Rethinking LLM Decoding as Ensemble Pruning
items.abstract: This paper proposes Mahalanobis-Ensemble Decoding (ME-Decoding), a new LLM decoding method that views token selection as pruning an ensemble of candidates. Unlike previous approaches that ignore semantic relationships between tokens, ME-Decoding uses Mahalanobis distance to identify and discount redundant candidates, promoting semantic diversity while maintaining high probability. This novel framework offers a more efficient and stable way to improve LLM generation quality.

items.title: Clueing up LLMs with Tool-Augmented Deductive Reasoning
items.abstract: This paper introduces a novel benchmark, a text-based Clue game, to evaluate multi-step deductive reasoning in LLMs. The core method involves instantiating LLM agents that play the game, requiring them to infer hidden information, maintain logical consistency, and update beliefs over multiple turns. The contribution lies in providing a challenging environment to test and improve LLMs' ability to perform complex, agentic deductive reasoning.
items.figure_caption: Example turn in Clue game environment with the possibility matrix tool highlighted; the matrix records Yes, No, and Maybe values for possible cards in other players’ hands.

items.title: Compositional Policy Violations: When Step-Level Compliance Fails In Agentic AI Workflows
items.abstract: This paper introduces "Compositional Policy Violations" (CPVs), a new failure mode in agentic AI workflows where individual steps comply with policies, but the overall execution violates them. The core method is defining and categorizing CPVs, highlighting the inadequacy of step-scoped governance for complex, multi-step policies. The contribution is identifying this critical gap and providing a framework for understanding and addressing these violations, which current step-level checks miss.

items.title: Reasoning through Evolution: Automatic Meta-path Discovery for LLM-based Fake News Detection
items.abstract: This paper proposes MAGER, a novel framework that uses a multi-agent genetic evolution approach to automatically discover optimal meta-paths within news propagation graphs. These discovered meta-paths effectively compress complex graph structures into informative subgraphs, overcoming the modality mismatch and information overload issues that hinder LLMs in fake news detection. This enables frozen LLMs to perform reliable structure-aware veracity reasoning, even in zero-shot and few-shot scenarios.

items.title: Rethinking Critic Learning in PPO: Understanding and Mitigating Value Flattening
items.abstract: This paper identifies "Value Flattening" as a failure mode in PPO critics for large language models, where estimated state values are overly smooth compared to actual returns. This phenomenon is linked to implicit variance penalties and redundant updates. The authors propose SP$^3$O, which applies the value loss to sparse, well-separated states to mitigate this issue and improve learning.

items.title: Which LLM is Best for Translating Natural Language Goals to PDDL
items.abstract: This paper investigates the effectiveness of Large Language Models (LLMs) in translating natural language testing goals into the formal PDDL language for automated planning. The core method involves a carefully designed prompt template to assess six state-of-the-art LLMs on accuracy, speed, and error rates using real-world benchmarks. The contribution is demonstrating that LLMs can reliably translate these goals with high accuracy, with Gemini 2.5 Flash and GPT-4.1 showing particular strengths.

items.title: Preventing Model Collapse: A Fisher-Rao Perspective on the Dynamics of Training with Synthetic Data
items.abstract: This paper provides a theoretical framework to prevent "model collapse" in LLMs trained on synthetic data. By analyzing training dynamics through the lens of Fisher-Rao geometry, it establishes rigorous guarantees on the minimum proportion of real human data needed to maintain training stability and prevent models from forgetting the true data distribution. This work offers a principled approach to determining the optimal balance between synthetic and human data for robust LLM training.

items.title: ScienceIDE: Turning World's Scientific Codebase into Agent Learnable Environments
items.abstract: ScienceIDE addresses the "scientific experience bottleneck" by transforming scientific code repositories into agent-learnable environments. Its core method involves agents, guided by expert-defined cases and criteria, converting code into executable environments for task generation, execution, and verification. The paper's contribution is this infrastructure and the resulting PhAI-IDE model family, which demonstrates improved scientific code repair and general reasoning capabilities.

items.title: Affora: A Design System for Agent-Friendly Interfaces
items.abstract: Affora is a design system that makes software interfaces understandable to both human users and computer agents. Its core method involves defining interaction meanings within interface components, allowing agents to interpret task states and actions while preserving visual design freedom for humans. The contribution is a set of principles, reusable implementations, and checks that improve agent performance and potentially reduce interaction costs, bridging the gap between user experience and agent accessibility.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. One interface, two kinds of reader. People and agents may act on the same application while receiving different representations of its controls, state, and possible actions. A left-to-right diagram comparing how a person and a computer-use agent perceive, reason about, and act on the same interface. The interface contains a visual skin and an underlying declared substrate. The person primarily perceives the rendered interface, while the agent may receive a DOM representation, accessibility tree, marked screenshot, or raw screenshot. Additional agent-only channels such as agent.md and WebMCP bypass parts of the shared interface.

items.title: Flag Game: A Toy Model for Mechanistic Swarm Interpretability
items.abstract: The Flag Game is a toy model designed to understand how AI agents form collective beliefs. Agents observe private data, share beliefs, and weigh social evidence to infer a hidden truth. The paper's contribution lies in demonstrating how this simple model reproduces complex emergent phenomena like performance scaling with population size and belief polarization, offering insights into mechanistic swarm interpretability.
items.figure_caption: The Flag Game (demo website: https://flag-game-demo.vercel.app ) exhibits rich collective phenomenology despite its simplicity. (a) A hidden flag is observed through private evidence; bounded agents exchange reports, and the system tracks agent’s country guess. (b–e) Collective mean accuracy (Sec. 3 ) under four controls: population size (b), social-awareness prompting (c), team diversity (d), and organizational structure (e).

items.summary: Mustafa Suleyman warns that as AI models become more capable, we must proactively consider their "welfare" to ensure responsible development and prevent unintended negative consequences.

items.title: Breaking the 1.58-bit Barrier for Ternary LLMs
items.summary: Researchers have achieved a breakthrough in ternary Large Language Models (LLMs), pushing past the 1.58-bit quantization barrier for improved efficiency and performance.

items.summary: DeepSeek v4.1 Flash has been released, and the company claims it's their most advanced model for hacking tasks.

items.summary: OpenSpec is a lightweight, configurable AI specification framework designed to streamline the development and management of AI models.

items.title: DeepSeek-v4.1 Flash: Pushing the Limits of KV Cache Compression
items.summary: DeepSeek-v4.1 Flash introduces a novel KV cache compression technique to significantly reduce memory usage and improve inference speed for large language models.

items.description: Fast, efficient, battle-tested at Alibaba's scale. Hybrid architecture code review tool: deterministic pipelines + LLM Agent, precise line-level comments, built-in multi-language ruleset (NPE, thread-safety, XSS, SQL injection), OpenAI & Anthropic compatible.
items.summary: This repository provides a fast, battle-tested hybrid code review tool for Alibaba's scale, combining deterministic pipelines with LLM agents for precise, line-level comments and built-in multi-language security rules.

items.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings

items.description: Tinycast — a tiny, fully native macOS launcher, hotkeys, and clipboard history.

items.summary: This repository provides open-source plugins designed to enhance Claude Cowork for knowledge workers, enabling them to integrate external tools and functionalities for improved productivity.

items.description: Ever® Gauzy™ - Open Business Management Platform (ERP/CRM/HRM/ATS/PM) - https://gauzy.co

items.summary: Anki is a powerful, open-source spaced repetition flashcard program designed for efficient memorization through customizable decks and intelligent scheduling.

This approach promotes stable training, prevents reward hacking, and fosters continuous reasoning growth, outperforming existing baselines on various benchmarks.
papers.figure_caption: Motivation of the STRETCH Framework. (a) Cognitive Zones: Comfort, stretch (optimal learning), and difficulty. (b) Paradigm Comparison: Top: static general questions leading to learner capability stagnation. Bottom: adaptive questions achieving dynamic difficulty matching via a learnable Scaffolder for progressive improving of Learner.

papers.title: Ask the Tool, Don't Guess: Agent Tool Calls Hold Their Progress, and the Serving System Should Read It
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the inefficiency of agent systems waiting for tool execution by proposing that tools explicitly report their progress. Instead of guessing tool durations, the system can dynamically manage GPU memory based on real-time progress signals. This approach recovers valuable KV cache memory without negatively impacting agent performance.

papers.title: ASLEval: Measuring Privacy Exposure Displacement in LLM Agent Sessions
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "privacy exposure displacement" to address limitations in evaluating LLM agent privacy. Their framework, ASLEval, measures the mismatch between local privacy checks and actual data exposure across multi-step sessions. This approach reveals significant privacy leaks missed by traditional methods, highlighting issues with outlet-only views and attacker reports.

papers.title: Beyond Outcomes: Dual-View Relational Learning for Efficient Agent Benchmarking
papers.abstract: This paper introduces DualViewEval, a novel method for compressing agent benchmarks. It addresses the high cost of evaluating agents by jointly learning from both final outcomes and complementary process signals observed in agent trajectories. This dual-view approach allows for more efficient and accurate prediction of full benchmark scores using a significantly smaller subset of tasks.

papers.title: Beyond Truncation: Rethinking LLM Decoding as Ensemble Pruning
papers.abstract: This paper proposes Mahalanobis-Ensemble Decoding (ME-Decoding), a new LLM decoding method that views token selection as pruning an ensemble of candidates. Unlike previous approaches that ignore semantic relationships between tokens, ME-Decoding uses Mahalanobis distance to identify and discount redundant candidates, promoting semantic diversity while maintaining high probability. This novel framework offers a more efficient and stable way to improve LLM generation quality.

papers.title: Clueing up LLMs with Tool-Augmented Deductive Reasoning
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel benchmark, a text-based Clue game, to evaluate multi-step deductive reasoning in LLMs. The core method involves instantiating LLM agents that play the game, requiring them to infer hidden information, maintain logical consistency, and update beliefs over multiple turns. The contribution lies in providing a challenging environment to test and improve LLMs' ability to perform complex, agentic deductive reasoning.
papers.figure_caption: Example turn in Clue game environment with the possibility matrix tool highlighted; the matrix records Yes, No, and Maybe values for possible cards in other players’ hands.

papers.title: Compositional Policy Violations: When Step-Level Compliance Fails In Agentic AI Workflows
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "Compositional Policy Violations" (CPVs), a new failure mode in agentic AI workflows where individual steps comply with policies, but the overall execution violates them. The core method is defining and categorizing CPVs, highlighting the inadequacy of step-scoped governance for complex, multi-step policies. The contribution is identifying this critical gap and providing a framework for understanding and addressing these violations, which current step-level checks miss.

papers.title: Reasoning through Evolution: Automatic Meta-path Discovery for LLM-based Fake News Detection
papers.abstract: This paper proposes MAGER, a novel framework that uses a multi-agent genetic evolution approach to automatically discover optimal meta-paths within news propagation graphs. These discovered meta-paths effectively compress complex graph structures into informative subgraphs, overcoming the modality mismatch and information overload issues that hinder LLMs in fake news detection. This enables frozen LLMs to perform reliable structure-aware veracity reasoning, even in zero-shot and few-shot scenarios.

papers.title: Rethinking Critic Learning in PPO: Understanding and Mitigating Value Flattening
papers.abstract: This paper identifies "Value Flattening" as a failure mode in PPO critics for large language models, where estimated state values are overly smooth compared to actual returns. This phenomenon is linked to implicit variance penalties and redundant updates. The authors propose SP$^3$O, which applies the value loss to sparse, well-separated states to mitigate this issue and improve learning.

papers.title: Which LLM is Best for Translating Natural Language Goals to PDDL
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the effectiveness of Large Language Models (LLMs) in translating natural language testing goals into the formal PDDL language for automated planning. The core method involves a carefully designed prompt template to assess six state-of-the-art LLMs on accuracy, speed, and error rates using real-world benchmarks. The contribution is demonstrating that LLMs can reliably translate these goals with high accuracy, with Gemini 2.5 Flash and GPT-4.1 showing particular strengths.

papers.title: Preventing Model Collapse: A Fisher-Rao Perspective on the Dynamics of Training with Synthetic Data
papers.abstract: This paper provides a theoretical framework to prevent "model collapse" in LLMs trained on synthetic data. By analyzing training dynamics through the lens of Fisher-Rao geometry, it establishes rigorous guarantees on the minimum proportion of real human data needed to maintain training stability and prevent models from forgetting the true data distribution. This work offers a principled approach to determining the optimal balance between synthetic and human data for robust LLM training.

papers.title: ScienceIDE: Turning World's Scientific Codebase into Agent Learnable Environments
papers.abstract: ScienceIDE addresses the "scientific experience bottleneck" by transforming scientific code repositories into agent-learnable environments. Its core method involves agents, guided by expert-defined cases and criteria, converting code into executable environments for task generation, execution, and verification. The paper's contribution is this infrastructure and the resulting PhAI-IDE model family, which demonstrates improved scientific code repair and general reasoning capabilities.

papers.title: Affora: A Design System for Agent-Friendly Interfaces
papers.abstract: Affora is a design system that makes software interfaces understandable to both human users and computer agents. Its core method involves defining interaction meanings within interface components, allowing agents to interpret task states and actions while preserving visual design freedom for humans. The contribution is a set of principles, reusable implementations, and checks that improve agent performance and potentially reduce interaction costs, bridging the gap between user experience and agent accessibility.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. One interface, two kinds of reader. People and agents may act on the same application while receiving different representations of its controls, state, and possible actions. A left-to-right diagram comparing how a person and a computer-use agent perceive, reason about, and act on the same interface. The interface contains a visual skin and an underlying declared substrate. The person primarily perceives the rendered interface, while the agent may receive a DOM representation, accessibility tree, marked screenshot, or raw screenshot. Additional agent-only channels such as agent.md and WebMCP bypass parts of the shared interface.

papers.title: Flag Game: A Toy Model for Mechanistic Swarm Interpretability
papers.abstract: The Flag Game is a toy model designed to understand how AI agents form collective beliefs. Agents observe private data, share beliefs, and weigh social evidence to infer a hidden truth. The paper's contribution lies in demonstrating how this simple model reproduces complex emergent phenomena like performance scaling with population size and belief polarization, offering insights into mechanistic swarm interpretability.
papers.figure_caption: The Flag Game (demo website: https://flag-game-demo.vercel.app ) exhibits rich collective phenomenology despite its simplicity. (a) A hidden flag is observed through private evidence; bounded agents exchange reports, and the system tracks agent’s country guess. (b–e) Collective mean accuracy (Sec. 3 ) under four controls: population size (b), social-awareness prompting (c), team diversity (d), and organizational structure (e).
